transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble with... well, with snacking. It's probably not a huge deal, I'm sure you see people with much bigger problems, but... what kind of worries me is that once I start picking at food late at night, I'll tell myself, "That's enough, Santiago." But then... my hand just keeps going back. It's almost like I don't get to make the decision anymore? I don't know if that makes sense, or if I'm explaining it right... is that the kind of thing you help people with here?
Do you feel like you're in control when you're eating during the day, or is it just at night that you feel like your hand keeps going back for food?

Oh, during the day I think I'm pretty good. I work in shipping and receiving, so I'm usually pretty busy on my feet and just eat a normal lunch on my break. I haven't really noticed it happening then... at least I don't think so. 

It's really just at night when I'm home. I mean, I'm sure everybody likes to unwind with a little snack in the evening, right? I just... maybe let it go a bit too far sometimes. I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing, I know it's probably just a bad habit. But yeah, daytime feels pretty normal and under control to me. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you usually feel guilty after these late-night snacking episodes?

Guilty? Um... I don't know if I'd use the word guilty, exactly. I mean... I don't want you to think I'm, you know, beating myself up over it or anything like that. 

It's more just... a little frustrating, maybe? Like I'll think, "Ah, Santiago, you did it again," but then I just clean up the wrappers and go to bed. I haven't really noticed feeling actual guilt about it, like I committed a crime or did something terrible. Just a little annoyed at myself for having a weak moment. 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong answer here. I just haven't really thought about it in those terms before. Is that... is that the kind of information you need?
Do you feel like you're eating very quickly or eating more than you intended to during these late-night snacking episodes?

Um, well... I guess I might eat a little faster than normal? I mean, it's not like I'm shoveling it in or anything crazy. It's just... you know, when I'm sitting down for dinner with the family, we take our time, we talk. But at night, when everyone else is asleep... I guess I just sort of hurry through it? 

It's almost like I want to finish it before anyone wakes up and comes into the kitchen. So I probably don't even really taste it as much as I should, since I'm just trying to get it done quietly. And yeah, I suppose I do end up eating a bit more than I planned when I opened the pantry. But it's just regular snack food, nothing too out of the ordinary. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these late-night snacking episodes?

Well, I mean... I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally out of control or anything. I'm a grown man, right? But... I guess what worries me a little bit is that once I start picking at the food, it's hard to just walk away. 

I'll tell myself, "Okay, that's enough, Santiago, time for bed," but... it's almost like my hand just keeps going back to the bag or the box. Like I don't really get to make the decision to stop anymore, even though I know I should. It's probably just a lack of willpower on my part, you know? I'm sure it's nothing too serious. 

But yeah, I guess it does feel a little hard to stop once I get going. Is that... is that normal for people who snack at night? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy here.
Do you ever feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during the day, like when you're having your normal lunch at work?

Oh, um... no, not really. During the day, I'm... I'm completely fine, actually. I mean, at work, I just have my regular lunch in the breakroom with the other guys from the warehouse. I eat my sandwich or whatever I packed, and then I just go right back out to the floor. 

I don't have any trouble stopping then. It's very routine, you know? I just eat my normal portion and I'm full, and I don't even really think about food again until my shift is over. I'm totally in control during the day, I promise. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means whatever I'm doing isn't too serious, since it's really just a nighttime thing for me. Does that... is that helpful for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you usually eat at night because you're feeling stressed, anxious, or bored?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I'm not really a stressed-out kind of guy, you know? My job is pretty steady, and I like keeping busy. And I wouldn't say I'm anxious or anything like that. 

I guess maybe sometimes it's just... I don't know, maybe a little bit of boredom? Like, the house is quiet, everyone's asleep, and I'm just sitting there watching TV. It's just something to do with my hands, I suppose. But I wouldn't say I'm eating because I'm upset or anything negative. 

It's just a little habit I've picked up, I think. A lot of guys my age probably do the same thing, right? Just having a little snack while watching a late-night game or a movie. I hope that makes sense. I just don't want you to think I'm, like, emotionally eating or anything serious like that. Does that sound like a normal reason to you?
Have you ever felt like you couldn't stop eating during a meal at work?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. Like I think I was saying just a little bit ago, work is... well, it's totally fine. I've never had that feeling during my shifts. 

I just eat what I brought and get right back out to the loading dock. There's no urge to keep going or anything like that. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. But yeah, work is a hundred percent normal for me. I wouldn't let myself get out of hand in front of the guys anyway, you know? 

Does that make sense for what you're looking for? I'm trying to give you the best answers I can.
Do you feel like you're eating more than you intended to during these late-night snacking episodes because you can't stop or because you're just really hungry?

Well, um... I guess I usually start out thinking I'm just a little hungry, you know? Just wanting a quick bite. But... I want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you, since you're trying to help me. 

I guess what worries me a little bit is that once I start picking at the food late at night, I'll actually tell myself, "Okay, that's enough, Santiago." Like, I know I should put it away. But... my hand just keeps going back for more. It almost feels like I don't get to make the decision anymore, if that makes sense? Like my brain says stop, but my hand just isn't listening. 

I know it probably sounds a little silly, a grown man saying he can't stop eating some chips or whatever. I really hope it doesn't make me sound too crazy or anything. I'm sure it's just a bad habit I need to break. Is that... does that answer what you were asking me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during the daytime, outside of your late-night snacking episodes?

Um, no... no, definitely not during the day. Like I was saying about work, I just have my regular lunch and that's it. I'm usually too busy moving around with the inventory and the trucks to even think about snacking, to be honest. 

So I've never felt out of control like that when the sun's up. It's really just... just that late-night thing when the house is quiet and I'm sitting still. I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means it's not too bad since I can manage perfectly fine during the daytime. Am I giving you the right kind of answers for what you need? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you feel like you're in control of how much you eat during these late-night snacking episodes?

Well, um... I guess it kind of goes back to what I was trying to explain just a little bit ago. And I really hate admitting this, because I like to think I'm a pretty together guy, you know? But... no, not really. 

During those late nights, I'll literally say out loud to myself, 'Santiago, that's enough, you don't need any more.' But my hand just keeps reaching into the bag anyway. It's like I'm not the one making the choice to keep eating, even though I'm the one doing it. 

I really hope I don't sound completely ridiculous repeating that. I definitely don't want you to think I'm totally out of control in my normal life or anything—it's really just those quiet moments at night. I just want to make sure I'm being as honest as you need me to be so you can do your job. Does that help answer your question?
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these late-night snacking episodes, even if it's just for a moment?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? But nothing too crazy, I promise. I mean, I think anyone would feel a little silly after eating too many chips, right? 

I guess sometimes I wake up the next morning and see the empty wrappers in the trash, and I feel a little... I don't know, a little foolish, maybe? Like I should have known better. But it's not like it ruins my whole day or anything. I just kind of brush it off and head to work. 

I know it's not the best habit, and I'm definitely going to try harder to stop. I really don't want you to think I'm sitting around beating myself up over it or anything. It's just a minor thing, really. Is that... is that normal? To just feel a little silly about it? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Is there a particular type of food that you tend to lose control with during these late-night snacking episodes?

Um, no, not really. It's not like I have this one specific weakness or anything. I mean, I guess whatever is just around in the pantry? 

Like I said, maybe some chips, or maybe some cookies if we have them... just normal snack stuff, you know? It's not like I'm going out of my way to buy anything special or... or going crazy over one specific kind of food. I just kind of grab whatever is easiest when I'm sitting there watching TV. 

I think that's pretty typical, right? Just eating whatever's convenient? I hope that's what you were asking. I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because it's really just normal pantry stuff. Does that make sense?
Do you usually eat at night because you're feeling relaxed and alone, or is it more related to other emotions or circumstances?

Well, um... I guess it's mostly just because it's quiet, you know? Like, the house is finally still, and I can just sit and unwind after a long day at the warehouse. 

I wouldn't say I'm eating because I'm upset or stressed or anything like that. I mean, sure, work can be tiring, but I'm a pretty easygoing guy. I don't really get all worked up about things. So, yeah, it's really just about relaxing. It's just me, the TV, and having a little snack to wind down. 

I think a lot of people do that, don't they? Just enjoy the peace and quiet with a snack? I really hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, because it's honestly just my way of relaxing at the end of the day. Is that helpful?
Do you find that you lose control over eating in situations other than late at night, such as during special occasions or holidays?

Um, no, not really. I mean, holidays are always a little... you know, everyone eats a bit more during Thanksgiving or whatever, right? But I wouldn't say I lose control or anything like that. 

When I'm around other people, like at a party or a family thing, I'm pretty good about just having a normal amount. I definitely don't go overboard when others are around. I'd hate for anyone to think I was being greedy or, you know, making a scene. So I just have a plate like everyone else and leave it at that. 

It's really just that quiet time at night when I'm by myself. During the day or at special events, I'm totally fine. I hope that's a good thing? Like, it means it's not a huge problem, right, if it's only happening when I'm alone watching TV?
Do you find that you lose control over eating with all types of food or just certain ones during these late-night episodes?

Well, um, I think it's kind of like what I was saying earlier... it's really just whatever happens to be in the house. I wouldn't say it's all types of food, like I'm not eating a whole meal or anything, and it's definitely not one specific thing I'm obsessed with. It's just... whatever is easy to grab out of the pantry. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a more specific answer for you. I just don't want to make it sound like I'm hoarding special junk food or doing anything too crazy. It's really just regular snacks, whatever is closest when I sit down. I'm trying to give you the best picture of it... does that help answer your question?
Do you ever feel like you lose control over eating at any other time of day besides late at night?

No, honestly, it's really just a nighttime thing. During the day, you know, I'm at the warehouse, I'm busy, I just eat a regular lunch with the guys. I don't even really think about food that much when I'm working or out and about. 

It's really only when I'm finally home and the day is done. I'd never do that kind of thing during the day anyway, I mean, I wouldn't want anyone at work to see me just eating and eating. That would be pretty embarrassing, right? So, yeah, it's strictly just my little way to unwind at night. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Do you feel like your late-night snacking is causing problems in your daily life or affecting your relationships with others?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's causing, like, *major* problems. I mean, I'm still getting to all my shifts at the warehouse on time, and I'm handling all the shipping and receiving stuff just fine. My boss hasn't noticed anything slipping, so that's good, right? 

But, um... I guess maybe it's affecting things just a tiny bit at home. Like, I've started sort of... avoiding going into the kitchen late at night if my family is still up in there. I just... I worry someone might notice that I'm acting a little uneasy or weird around the food, you know? I really don't want them to think less of me or worry about me. So I just kind of steer clear until they go to bed. 

It's nothing huge, though! I'm still doing what I need to do during the day. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight or overall physical health since you started having these late-night snacking episodes?

Um, no, not really. I mean... maybe my weight fluctuates a pound or two here and there, just like anyone's, but nothing major. I haven't had to go out and buy new work pants or anything like that. And physically, you know, I feel totally fine. I'm still lifting heavy boxes and moving pallets around at the warehouse without getting winded or having any trouble, so it definitely hasn't slowed me down. 

So, yeah, I'd say my overall health is still pretty good. I hope that's a good sign, right? Like, maybe it means I'm not doing too much damage with the snacking. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly... does that help give you a better idea of where I'm at?
Do you think you eat at night as a way to cope with any emotions or feelings?

Um, no, I really don't think so. I'm not, like, a super emotional guy or anything. I mean, work gets busy, sure, but I leave it at the warehouse when I clock out. I don't come home feeling stressed out or upset or anything like that. 

Honestly, I think it's just... well, I just really like the food, and it's become a little bit of a habit to just snack while I watch TV and relax. I definitely wouldn't say I'm eating because I'm sad or angry. I hope that's a good thing, right? Like, maybe it just means it's a bad habit rather than some deep emotional issue. Does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm on the right track for you.
